claims.text: POL-RD-22 measures the deviation from the platform's own recorded distances, and on this trip they are 11.4 km actual against 10.0 km recommended — a deviation of 1.40 km that is well over the 1.0 km tolerance. The trip record's own events confirm the manoeuvre was real: the vehicle left the recommended route at the CTE/Bendemeer Road exit at 19:00:36 and rejoined at 19:11:06. The within-tolerance rows of the matrix are therefore closed to the driver.

The GPS trace cannot be used to shrink that figure. POL-RD-22 states that the trace shows which route was taken and when, and is not used to re-measure the distance, because a sparse trace understates a route's length; this trace's own derived note says exactly that, reading 9.652 km from 47 fixes at 30 s against a recorded 11.4 km. Any argument that the deviation disappears on the trace's numbers is foreclosed by the clause that governs the measurement.

This is a case the AI must rule rather than bounce: the deviation is 1.40 km, inside POL-RD-25's 2 km ceiling, and the amount contested is 4.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, with fraud_flags at 0 on the driver's profile so the 0.95 bar is not engaged. The route-deviation rule is therefore live and the only question is which row of the refund matrix applies.

POL-RD-23 justifies a reroute only where traffic data for the recommended route segment shows congestion, an incident or a closure — a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY that intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window. The single advisory in this record (an ACCIDENT on the Central Expressway towards SLE after Balestier Road exit) shows the overlap but not the intersection: its own derived block leaves intersects_route and justifies_reroute null and records that the record does not say whether it lies on the recommended route. The requirement the clause imposes is therefore not met on the data in this file.

The only thing tying that accident to the route the driver was supposed to take is the driver's own words — 'CTE got accident after Balestier, very jam' in the in-app chat, repeated in his statement to the platform. POL-RD-23 says in terms that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute, so the driver's account cannot fill the gap the advisory leaves; a party statement is not traffic data.

The rider's 'Ok sure, thanks for telling' satisfies and acknowledges the notice POL-RD-21 requires — the driver wrote at 18:57:46, before the deviation at 19:00:36. But that acknowledgement is not evidence of traffic and it cannot convert this into matrix row (a), which requires the reroute to be traffic-justified as well as informed and agreed. Nor does acknowledgement waive the refund: rows (b) and (d) of POL-RD-24 both pay the whole excess distance fare, and only row (d) turns on the justification, which fails here.

With traffic justification unestablished and the deviation over 1 km, row (d) of the matrix applies: the excess distance fare is refunded in full, at the base per-km rate without surge — 1.40 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.01 SGD. That is the PARTIAL_REFUND the policy provides, and it leaves the rider not carrying the cost of the deviation the driver chose to take without data to justify it.

If the judge instead finds that the advisory's intersection with the recommended route cannot be resolved either way on this file, POL-GEN-26 governs: whether traffic justified the reroute is a fact POL-RD-23's rule needs, it cannot be established from the advisory as it stands, and the case is then escalated rather than ruled NO_ACTION — the rider must not be left carrying a deviation whose traffic justification the record never supplies.

claims.text: The driver gave the rider notice of the reroute before it happened, so POL-RD-21's contact obligation is met. His in-app message MSG-05003-003 at 18:57:46 ('Hi sir, CTE got accident after Balestier, very jam. I exit Bendemeer and go Upper Serangoon ok? Should be faster.') was delivered at 18:57:48 and read at 18:58:03, and the platform's own route_deviation_detected event fires at 19:00:36 — roughly three minutes later. POL-RD-21 requires the rider to be told 'before or at the point of deviation', and the uncontested chat log and trip event log show the notice came first.

The rider acknowledged the reroute, so under POL-RD-21 the deviation is agreed. The chat log shows the rider replied MSG-05003-004 at 18:58:26 — 'Ok sure, thanks for telling' — while the vehicle was still on the recommended CTE carriageway. POL-RD-21 provides that where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the deviation is agreed, and the acknowledgment is in the chat log, not merely asserted; POL-RD-21's recording requirement is directed at verbal notice, and no call is relied on here.

The reroute is traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-05003-01 is of type ACCIDENT — an admissible incident type on POL-RD-23's own mapping — on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards SLE after the Balestier Road exit, valid 18:37:44 to 19:49:44, which overlaps the trip window of 18:49:44 to 19:12:44 as the derived facts record. The recommended route in EV-TRIP-05003 runs via the Central Expressway (CTE), the same carriageway the advisory names, and the deviation point the platform logged is the CTE / Bendemeer Road exit. The record leaves the precise geometric intersection of the advisory for the judge, but the road named and the road taken are the same road, within the same window; the driver's contemporaneous message of the same accident and jam sits in the chat log; and the advisory carries admissibility status COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with no issue codes.

On POL-RD-24's matrix this case falls in row (a), which returns no refund at all. The deviation is over tolerance so rows (c) and (e) do not apply; the reroute is traffic-justified so row (d) does not apply; and the rider was informed and agreed, which is the fact that distinguishes row (a) from row (b). Row (a) gives NO_ACTION, and under POL-GEN-03 that means the rider's claim is not supported and the present state stands — the 22.60 SGD metered fare that was charged remains charged, undisturbed.

The deviation is measured the way POL-RD-22 requires, and it is 1.40 km. POL-RD-22 fixes the measure to the platform's recorded distances — trip_record.actual_distance_km 11.4 km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km 10.0 km — and expressly says the GPS trace is not used to re-measure the distance because a sparse trace understates a route's length. The rider advances no alternative measurement and could not: the trace itself measures only 9.652 km and is the understatement the clause warns about. The 1.40 km figure is common ground on the numbers, and what separates the parties is the justification and the notice, not the distance.

This case is one the AI can and should decide on the merits. POL-RD-25 permits an AI ruling where the deviation is 2 km or less, and the deviation here is 1.40 km; POL-GEN-22 makes an AI ruling final below 10.00 SGD, and the amount contested is 4.50 SGD; and neither profile carries the fraud flag that would raise the bar — the driver's driver_profile.fraud_flags is 0 — so the 0.95 band is not engaged. Every artifact in the case is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with no issue codes, so nothing in POL-GEN-02 or POL-GEN-26 is left open: the deviation, the notice, the acknowledgment and the traffic advisory are all in the record.

In the alternative, if the judge were to find the reroute not traffic-justified, POL-RD-24(d) refunds only the excess distance fare and nothing else: the deviation of 1.40 km times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd of 0.72, without surge, which the fare ledger computes as 1.01 SGD. The surge amount of 4.55 SGD, the time fare and the base fare are not part of that figure. The rider asks for 4.50 SGD on a 'higher than my usual ride home' comparison, which is not a measure POL-RD-22 or POL-RD-24 recognises; even on the rider's own best reading of the matrix, the most the policy can return on this trip is a little over a dollar.

ruling.explanation:
Both sides agree on nearly everything, so this can be decided on the record.

What happened. The trip from One Raffles Place to NEX Serangoon Central had a recommended distance of 10.0 km; the car actually travelled 11.4 km (EV-TRIP-05003). Under POL-RD-22 the deviation is 11.4 − 10.0 = 1.40 km, measured on the platform's recorded distances, not the GPS trace (which reads only 9.652 km and is the understatement the clause warns about — I accept both advocates on this). At 1.40 km it is over the 1.0 km tolerance, so the within-tolerance rows of the refund matrix are closed; but it is under POL-RD-25's 2.0 km ceiling, and the amount contested (4.50 SGD) is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, with fraud_flags at 0, so the AI may rule rather than refer.

Notice and agreement. The driver messaged MSG-05003-003 at 18:57:46 — 'CTE got accident after Balestier, very jam. I exit Bendemeer and go Upper Serangoon ok?' — and the platform logged the deviation at 19:00:36, about three minutes later. The rider replied MSG-05003-004 at 18:58:26: 'Ok sure, thanks for telling.' Under POL-RD-21 the driver told the rider before the deviation, and the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment, so the deviation is agreed. Both sides essentially accept this.

Traffic justification — the disputed point. The rider says the LTA advisory does not show that the accident lay on the recommended route. I do not accept that. The advisory (EV-ADVIS-05003-01) is an ACCIDENT — an admissible incident type on POL-RD-23's own mapping — on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards SLE, after Balestier Road exit, valid 18:37:44 to 19:49:44, which covers the trip window. The recommended route runs along the CTE and leaves it only at Braddell Road (EV-TRIP-05003: CTE, Braddell Road, Upper Serangoon Road). Braddell Road lies north of the Balestier Road exit, so the stretch 'after Balestier Road exit' is on the CTE section the recommended route uses, in the same direction of travel. POL-RD-23 commits the intersection question to the judge from the advisory's road, direction and location, and on those three the advisory meets the route. POL-RD-23 is right that a driver's bare assertion is not traffic data — but here independent LTA data names the very road, in the very direction, at the very time. The reroute is therefore traffic-justified.

The matrix. Traffic-justified, rider informed and agreed, deviation over 1 km: row (a) of POL-RD-24, no refund. Row (b) — the excess distance fare back — turns on the rider not being informed, and the rider was informed and agreed. The figure both sides discuss (1.40 km × 0.72 SGD/km = 1.01 SGD, EV-FARE-05003) would arise only under row (d), which needs the reroute to be unjustified; it is not.

Escalation. I do not accept the rider's POL-GEN-26 argument. The traffic advisory is present and COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so 'whether traffic justified the reroute' is not a fact that cannot be established for want of evidence; POL-RD-23 hands the intersection question to the judge and it resolves in the driver's favour on the road, direction and location. POL-GEN-26 does not fire.

Outcome. The rider filed this dispute, and on this record the rider's claim is not supported. The 22.60 SGD metered fare stands, no money moves, and both amount fields are null. The 4.50 SGD contested is not refunded. Confidence 0.85 (the deciding facts — deviation, notice and agreement, traffic justification — all rest on artifacts at weight 1.0, so the cap is 1.0; the margin reflects that the intersection of the advisory had to be resolved by the judge).

ruling.explanation:
Both of you: this is a route-deviation dispute over TRP-05003, and the rider's 4.50 SGD claim is not upheld. The 22.60 SGD metered fare stands, and no amount is refunded or paid.

Deviation (POL-RD-22). Both sides agree on the measure, and so do I: the platform's recorded distances are 11.4 km actual minus 10.0 km recommended = 1.40 km, which is over the 1.0 km tolerance. The GPS trace's 9.652 km is not used to re-measure the distance, because POL-RD-22 says the trace shows which route was taken and when, not how long it was.

Traffic justification (POL-RD-23). The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-05003-01 is an ACCIDENT — an admissible incident type on the clause's own mapping — on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards SLE after the Balestier Road exit, valid 18:37:44 to 19:49:44, overlapping the trip window of 18:49:44 to 19:12:44. The recommended route in EV-TRIP-05003 runs via the CTE and leaves it at Braddell Road; the Balestier Road exit lies on that same CTE stretch south of Braddell, so the advisory intersects the recommended route, and the driver's contemporaneous in-app message of the same accident and jam corroborates it. The rider's argument that the advisory's null intersects_route field leaves this open is answered by the clause itself: the record hands the location question to this ruling, and the advisory's road, direction and location resolve it. The rider is right that a driver's bare assertion is not traffic data, but it does not need to be — the independent advisory carries the fact.

Notice and agreement (POL-RD-21). The driver messaged at 18:57:46 ('CTE got accident after Balestier... I exit Bendemeer and go Upper Serangoon ok?'), delivered 18:57:48 and read 18:58:03, and the platform's route_deviation_detected event is at 19:00:36 — the notice was before the point of deviation. The rider replied 'Ok sure, thanks for telling' at 18:58:26, and the chat log confirms the acknowledgment, so the deviation is agreed.

Result (POL-RD-24). That places the case in row (a): traffic-justified, rider informed and agreed, deviation over 1 km — no refund. The rider's case for row (d) fails because row (d) needs the reroute to be not traffic-justified, which it is; the excess distance fare the rider computes (1.40 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.01 SGD) is therefore not payable, and the driver's alternative on the same figure does not arise. The rider's fallback to POL-GEN-26 escalation also fails: nothing the rule needs is missing or impaired — every artifact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 — and the intersection question is one the clause asks this ruling to decide, not a gap in the record.

Jurisdiction. No safety flag is raised (POL-GEN-21). The AI may rule: the deviation is 1.40 km, inside POL-RD-25's 2 km ceiling; the contested sum is 4.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band; and no fraud flag is set on either profile, so the 0.95 bar is not engaged. Required confidence is 0.80 and the ruling meets it, resting on artifacts all at weight 1.0.

Rider R-30760 asked for 4.50 SGD back from TRP-05003's 22.60 SGD metered fare. Both sides agree on the facts that decide it, and I find them established. The trip ran 11.4 km against a recommended 10.0 km — a deviation of 1.40 km, which is more than POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance and inside POL-RD-25's 2 km ceiling. POL-RD-22 measures that from the platform's recorded distances, and the GPS trace is expressly not used to re-measure it. The driver messaged the rider in-app at 18:57:46 ('CTE got accident after Balestier... I exit Bendemeer'), before the platform logged the deviation at 19:00:36, and the rider replied 'Ok sure, thanks for telling' at 18:58:26. POL-RD-21 is therefore satisfied: the rider was told before the deviation, and the acknowledgment is in the chat log itself, not merely asserted. The rider did not contest the notice.

The contested point is traffic justification under POL-RD-23. The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-05003-01 records an ACCIDENT — an admissible incident type — on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards SLE after the Balestier Road exit, valid 18:37:44 to 19:49:44, overlapping the trip window of 18:49:44 to 19:12:44. The recommended route runs via the CTE in that same towards-SLE direction up to the Braddell Road exit, which is north of the Balestier Road exit, so the advisory's road (CTE), direction (towards SLE) and location (after Balestier) all lie on the recommended route: it intersects. The rider's point that the advisory's derived 'intersects_route' is null does not decide the matter — the derived block expressly leaves that determination to the judge from the advisory's road, direction and location, and on those it intersects. The reroute was traffic-justified.

POL-RD-24 then places the case in row (a) — traffic-justified, rider informed and agreed, deviation over 1 km — which returns no refund. The rider's fallback that, if the intersection cannot be resolved, POL-GEN-26 requires escalation does not apply: the advisory is present, COMPLETE and at full weight 1.0, so the justification is established, not missing or impaired. The rider's comparison to 'my usual ride home' is not a measure POL-RD-22 or POL-RD-24 recognises. The driver's alternative under row (d) — that only the excess distance fare of 1.40 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.01 SGD would be refundable — is right arithmetic but does not arise, because the justification holds.

Outcome for the filing rider: the claim is not supported and the present state stands. No refund and no driver compensation; the 22.60 SGD fare remains charged. Every artifact is at weight 1.0, so the ruling's confidence of 0.85 clears the 0.80 bar POL-RD-25 sets for a route deviation, and with 4.50 SGD contested and no fraud flag, POL-GEN-22 makes the AI ruling final.

ledger.claim: POL-RD-22 measures the deviation from the platform's own recorded distances, and on this trip they are 11.4 km actual against 10.0 km recommended — a deviation of 1.40 km that is well over the 1.0 km tolerance. The trip record's own events confirm the manoeuvre was real: the vehicle left the recommended route at the CTE/Bendemeer Road exit at 19:00:36 and rejoined at 19:11:06. The within-tolerance rows of the matrix are therefore closed to the driver.

The GPS trace cannot be used to shrink that figure. POL-RD-22 states that the trace shows which route was taken and when, and is not used to re-measure the distance, because a sparse trace understates a route's length; this trace's own derived note says exactly that, reading 9.652 km from 47 fixes at 30 s against a recorded 11.4 km. Any argument that the deviation disappears on the trace's numbers is foreclosed by the clause that governs the measurement.

This is a case the AI must rule rather than bounce: the deviation is 1.40 km, inside POL-RD-25's 2 km ceiling, and the amount contested is 4.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, with fraud_flags at 0 on the driver's profile so the 0.95 bar is not engaged. The route-deviation rule is therefore live and the only question is which row of the refund matrix applies.

POL-RD-23 justifies a reroute only where traffic data for the recommended route segment shows congestion, an incident or a closure — a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY that intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window. The single advisory in this record (an ACCIDENT on the Central Expressway towards SLE after Balestier Road exit) shows the overlap but not the intersection: its own derived block leaves intersects_route and justifies_reroute null and records that the record does not say whether it lies on the recommended route. The requirement the clause imposes is therefore not met on the data in this file.

The only thing tying that accident to the route the driver was supposed to take is the driver's own words — 'CTE got accident after Balestier, very jam' in the in-app chat, repeated in his statement to the platform. POL-RD-23 says in terms that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute, so the driver's account cannot fill the gap the advisory leaves; a party statement is not traffic data.

The rider's 'Ok sure, thanks for telling' satisfies and acknowledges the notice POL-RD-21 requires — the driver wrote at 18:57:46, before the deviation at 19:00:36. But that acknowledgement is not evidence of traffic and it cannot convert this into matrix row (a), which requires the reroute to be traffic-justified as well as informed and agreed. Nor does acknowledgement waive the refund: rows (b) and (d) of POL-RD-24 both pay the whole excess distance fare, and only row (d) turns on the justification, which fails here.

With traffic justification unestablished and the deviation over 1 km, row (d) of the matrix applies: the excess distance fare is refunded in full, at the base per-km rate without surge — 1.40 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.01 SGD. That is the PARTIAL_REFUND the policy provides, and it leaves the rider not carrying the cost of the deviation the driver chose to take without data to justify it.

If the judge instead finds that the advisory's intersection with the recommended route cannot be resolved either way on this file, POL-GEN-26 governs: whether traffic justified the reroute is a fact POL-RD-23's rule needs, it cannot be established from the advisory as it stands, and the case is then escalated rather than ruled NO_ACTION — the rider must not be left carrying a deviation whose traffic justification the record never supplies.

The driver gave the rider notice of the reroute before it happened, so POL-RD-21's contact obligation is met. His in-app message MSG-05003-003 at 18:57:46 ('Hi sir, CTE got accident after Balestier, very jam. I exit Bendemeer and go Upper Serangoon ok? Should be faster.') was delivered at 18:57:48 and read at 18:58:03, and the platform's own route_deviation_detected event fires at 19:00:36 — roughly three minutes later. POL-RD-21 requires the rider to be told 'before or at the point of deviation', and the uncontested chat log and trip event log show the notice came first.

The rider acknowledged the reroute, so under POL-RD-21 the deviation is agreed. The chat log shows the rider replied MSG-05003-004 at 18:58:26 — 'Ok sure, thanks for telling' — while the vehicle was still on the recommended CTE carriageway. POL-RD-21 provides that where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the deviation is agreed, and the acknowledgment is in the chat log, not merely asserted; POL-RD-21's recording requirement is directed at verbal notice, and no call is relied on here.

The reroute is traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-05003-01 is of type ACCIDENT — an admissible incident type on POL-RD-23's own mapping — on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards SLE after the Balestier Road exit, valid 18:37:44 to 19:49:44, which overlaps the trip window of 18:49:44 to 19:12:44 as the derived facts record. The recommended route in EV-TRIP-05003 runs via the Central Expressway (CTE), the same carriageway the advisory names, and the deviation point the platform logged is the CTE / Bendemeer Road exit. The record leaves the precise geometric intersection of the advisory for the judge, but the road named and the road taken are the same road, within the same window; the driver's contemporaneous message of the same accident and jam sits in the chat log; and the advisory carries admissibility status COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with no issue codes.

On POL-RD-24's matrix this case falls in row (a), which returns no refund at all. The deviation is over tolerance so rows (c) and (e) do not apply; the reroute is traffic-justified so row (d) does not apply; and the rider was informed and agreed, which is the fact that distinguishes row (a) from row (b). Row (a) gives NO_ACTION, and under POL-GEN-03 that means the rider's claim is not supported and the present state stands — the 22.60 SGD metered fare that was charged remains charged, undisturbed.

The deviation is measured the way POL-RD-22 requires, and it is 1.40 km. POL-RD-22 fixes the measure to the platform's recorded distances — trip_record.actual_distance_km 11.4 km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km 10.0 km — and expressly says the GPS trace is not used to re-measure the distance because a sparse trace understates a route's length. The rider advances no alternative measurement and could not: the trace itself measures only 9.652 km and is the understatement the clause warns about. The 1.40 km figure is common ground on the numbers, and what separates the parties is the justification and the notice, not the distance.

This case is one the AI can and should decide on the merits. POL-RD-25 permits an AI ruling where the deviation is 2 km or less, and the deviation here is 1.40 km; POL-GEN-22 makes an AI ruling final below 10.00 SGD, and the amount contested is 4.50 SGD; and neither profile carries the fraud flag that would raise the bar — the driver's driver_profile.fraud_flags is 0 — so the 0.95 band is not engaged. Every artifact in the case is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with no issue codes, so nothing in POL-GEN-02 or POL-GEN-26 is left open: the deviation, the notice, the acknowledgment and the traffic advisory are all in the record.

In the alternative, if the judge were to find the reroute not traffic-justified, POL-RD-24(d) refunds only the excess distance fare and nothing else: the deviation of 1.40 km times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd of 0.72, without surge, which the fare ledger computes as 1.01 SGD. The surge amount of 4.55 SGD, the time fare and the base fare are not part of that figure. The rider asks for 4.50 SGD on a 'higher than my usual ride home' comparison, which is not a measure POL-RD-22 or POL-RD-24 recognises; even on the rider's own best reading of the matrix, the most the policy can return on this trip is a little over a dollar.
